item.title: Solving the Mysteries of Southeast Asia’s Prehistory
item.description: Archeologist Dougald O’Reilly speaks about his work on Laos' Plain of Jars and tracing the region's pre-historical societies.

item.title: Is Indonesia’s Nickel Production Cut Deliberately Undermining the Philippines’ Downstream Plans?
item.description: Indonesia’s production restrictions strengthen its position as a regional agenda setter. The Philippines, by contrast, risks becoming a price taker, bearing environmental pressures and reserve depletion while much of the value added occurs abroad.

item.title: ISKP’s Desperate Attacks Expose Its Weakness
item.description: The attack at a Shia Mosque in Islamabad seems aimed at fueling Shia-Sunni sectarian flames to attract former Lashkar-e-Jhangvi militants to its ranks.

item.title: Bangladesh’s Make or Break Election
item.description: Discussing the competing electoral alliances, the long shadow of the Awami League, and the challenges that the new government will face.

item.title: Sheikh Hasina on the ‘Most Perilous Chapter’ in Bangladesh’s History Since 1971
item.description: “You cannot organize credible elections while banning the country's largest political party, the Awami League.”

item.title: Is This the End of Pacifism in Japan?
item.description: The results from the February 8 election suggest that the long-standing debate over Japan’s defense policy has largely been settled.

item.title: What the History of China-Russia Relations May Tell Us About Their Future
item.description: As China’s history shows, no matter if it is Tsarist, Bolshevik, Soviet, or “democratic,” Russia’s strategic and geopolitical logic guiding its behavior remain unchanged.

item.title: How a 1942 Coal Mine Tragedy Became a Litmus Test for Japan-South Korea Relations
item.description: The latest leaders’ summit raised hopes for a recovery effort at Chosei Coal Mine. Now the death of a Taiwanese diver has put the project into question once again.

item.title: Can South Korea’s Cultural Industries Become Its New Growth Engine?
item.description: It’s not just about soft power – South Korea’s cultural exports are now emerging as a pillar of the national economy.

item.title: Citing ‘Unity,’ Kyrgyz President Japarov Dismisses Key Ally, Security Chief Tashiev
item.description: The surprise dismissal comes while Tashiev is reportedly out of the country.
